findings.title: Making .small-action a flex container breaks the floated button and avatar
findings.body: `.small-action` now gets `display: flex` (line 264), but its children are still positioned with floats. `button { float: right; }` (line 309) and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) stop working, because `float` has no effect on flex items. The action button (e.g. undo/delete on small action posts) will no longer sit at the right edge; it will appear right after the description text. The trailing `clear: both` (line 312) is also a leftover from the float layout. Fix: give the button `margin-left: auto` (or put `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) and drop the dead float rules.

findings.title: Header panel right-alignment relies on auto margins, which the old -webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks ignore
findings.body: The `flexbox()` mixin emits the legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` values as fallbacks. The panel is now pushed right only by `margin-left: auto` (line 37), since its `float: right` was removed. The 2009 box model does not distribute auto margins, so any browser that falls back to the legacy box display shows the panel (notifications, user menu) next to the logo instead of at the right. Either drop the legacy prefixes or keep a fallback such as `-webkit-box-pack: justify` or a flexible spacer.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items property
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` (line 121) was never a real property; IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above. The extra declaration is dead output repeated everywhere the mixin is used and should be removed.

findings.title: PR title/description do not match the change
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance" but its description is only "Test 5". The change is a layout refactor from floats to flexbox across the header, small-action posts and category badges, with visual side effects. There is no performance work and no explanation or screenshots for reviewers. The description should state what layouts change and how they were verified.
